sections.title: Learning objectives
sections.lede: These are the three things you will be able to do by the end of the lesson.

sections.title: The big picture
sections.lede: University German is full of fixed phrases, abbreviations and a slightly formal tone.

blocks.text: When you contact a lecturer, use Sie and the title: “Sehr geehrte Frau Professorin Weber”. State your course and your question early, then keep the email short. A standard opening is “Ich schreibe Ihnen wegen …”.

University life has its own vocabulary: die Anmeldung (registration), die Vorlesung (lecture), das Seminar, die Frist (deadline), der Dozent / die Dozentin. Abbreviations such as “WiSe” (winter semester) and “SoSe” (summer semester) appear on almost every timetable.

blocks.title: Ask early, ask clearly
blocks.text: Lecturers receive many emails. Put the course name and your question in the first two lines, and use a specific subject line.

sections.title: Rules & patterns
sections.lede: The patterns to keep in mind while you work through the examples.

rows: Die Anmeldung zum Kurs ist bis Freitag möglich.
Die Vorlesung findet am Dienstag statt.
Ich würde gern einen Termin mit Ihnen vereinbaren.

items: Use “findet statt” for scheduled events: Die Vorlesung findet um zehn Uhr statt.
“Bis wann?” asks for a deadline; “Ab wann?” asks when something starts.
Use “Ich hätte eine Frage zu …” to open a request politely.

sections.title: Example sentences
sections.lede: Notice how the pattern behaves in a complete sentence.

items.de: Ich würde gern einen Termin mit Ihnen vereinbaren.
items.en: I would like to arrange an appointment with you.
items.note: Würde gern is a polite way to ask.

items.de: Die Anmeldung ist bis Freitag möglich.
Die Vorlesung findet im Raum 3.12 statt.
items.en: The lecture takes place in room 3.12.
items.note: Findet … statt is the standard phrase for scheduled events.

items.de: Ich hätte eine Frage zur Hausarbeit.
items.en: I have a question about the term paper.
items.note: Zur is the contracted form of zu der.

sections.title: Pronunciation
sections.lede: Short, focused sound work. Play each item and repeat it twice.

blocks.text: German universities expect students to read the course description and the timetable before asking. A question that is already answered in the syllabus may get a short reply.
Office hours (“Sprechstunde”) are the normal place for longer questions. Sign up if required, arrive on time, and bring your documents.

lines.de: Könnten Sie mir bitte bestätigen, dass die Frist am 30. Juni endet?

sections.title: Grammar spotlight
sections.heading: University phrases
sections.lede: Learn the fixed phrases that appear in every course description.

rows: Ich würde gern einen Termin vereinbaren.
I would like to arrange an appointment.

blocks.text: Use zu + dative for topics: eine Frage zur Hausarbeit, zur Prüfung, zum Seminar. The forms are zur (feminine) and zum (masculine/neuter).

sections.tip: When you write to a lecturer, include the course name in the subject line. It helps them answer faster.

sections.title: Choose the right answer
sections.lede: Choose the answer that fits the sentence or the rule.

exercises.explanation: The separable verb is findet … statt, with statt at the end.
Bis marks the end of a period or deadline.
Hausarbeit is feminine, so zu der contracts to zur.

exercises.prompt: Which phrase is the most polite way to ask for a meeting?
options: Ich würde gern einen Termin vereinbaren.
Du musst mir einen Termin geben.
exercises.explanation: Würde gern is polite and appropriate for a lecturer.

sections.title: Speaking
sections.lede: Record or say your answer aloud, then compare it with the model.
sections.prompt: Ask a lecturer for an appointment about a term paper. Include a subject line and a polite request.

model.de: Betreff: Frage zur Hausarbeit. Sehr geehrte Frau Professorin Weber, ich hätte eine Frage zur Hausarbeit. Ich würde gern einen Termin mit Ihnen vereinbaren. Wann haben Sie Zeit?
model.en: Subject: Question about the term paper. Dear Professor Weber, I have a question about the term paper. I would like to arrange an appointment with you. When do you have time?

tips: Use the lecturer’s title and surname.
State the course and the topic in the first two lines.
Use würde gern for a polite request.

sections.title: Common mistakes
sections.lede: These are the errors learners most often make with this pattern.

items.right: Die Vorlesung findet am Dienstag statt.
items.why: Stattfinden is separable and needs its prefix at the end.

items.wrong: Ich habe eine Frage zu der Hausarbeit.
items.right: Ich habe eine Frage zur Hausarbeit.
items.why: In everyday German, zu der contracts to zur.
A specific date takes am, not bis.
